articles.content: New Models from StepFun and MiniMax Are Sending the Internet into a Tailspin Kilo Blog Subscribe Sign in New Models from StepFun and MiniMax Are Sending the Internet into a Tailspin And one of them is currently free in Kilo Ari Messer Jun 01, 2026 8 Share Model releases are coming at us faster than ever. Over the weekend, StepFun and MiniMax, two of the most prevalent Chinese model labs, dropped exciting new releases: Step 3.7 Flash and MiniMax M3 . To make things ever more intense: both labs released these new models out of the gate with open weights . The new StepFun model comes with a permissive Apache 2.0 license and MiniMax is expected to release the weights for M3 shortly. The internet is already buzzing—our community Discord and X feeds are in a tailspin over the agentic capabilitie

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: Then MiniMax M3 turned every head in the timeline. The first open-weight model to combine all three frontier capabilities in one system: a 1M-token context window, frontier coding and agentic performance, and native multimodality. The trick is MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA), which cuts per-token compute at 1M context to roughly 1/20th of the last generation. That's 9x faster pre-filling and 15x faster decoding.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: First up: Step 3.7 Flash, and it's **FREE** in Kilo right now. 196B params, but it sparsely activates only ~11B per token, so it stays fast even at long context. 256K window, selectable reasoning tiers (high/med/low), built for agentic coding and tool calling. Early testers are calling it "as good as Gemini Flash 3.0 at half the cost."

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: The open-weight labs did not come to play this week. StepFun dropped Step 3.7 Flash. MiniMax dropped M3. Both with open weights, both already live in Kilo. The "model wars" just got a lot more interesting.
